key_insight: In perovskite oxides for CO2-to-CH4 conversion, unoccupied TM 3d-band center, charge-transfer energy, and the W3d/W2p bandwidth ratio all correlate negatively with methane activity, with W3d/W2p emerging as the most useful descriptor.
engineering_relevance: A simple electronic-structure descriptor can guide high-throughput screening of double perovskites to prioritize compositions with higher predicted CO2 conversion activity.
method: Evaluated six electronic-structure descriptors linked to band centers and bandwidths.
Used parametric brute-force searching to fit explicit activity equations.
Screened 24 La-based double perovskites to identify promising candidates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent qualitative trends across descriptors and a selected fitting equation based only on W3d/W2p that was applied successfully for materials screening.
watch_item: The descriptor-activity relations are derived from correlations and fitted equations, so predictions may not generalize beyond the tested perovskite chemistry without further validation.
paper_title: Electronic Structure Descriptors for CO$_2$ Conversion Activity in Perovskite Oxides
